environment: Hervey Bay's humpback super pods steal the spring show
Reef Check volunteers report encouraging coral signs ahead of spawning season
science: Aussie researchers edge closer to cheaper, more efficient solar cells
sports: Queensland clubs gear up for finals fever across the AFL and NRL
stories.overview: Humpback whales turn the Queensland coast into a spring spectacular

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, it's Friday the fourth of September and mate, spring has well and truly sprung. I'm Alex Mercer, and as always I've got my partner in good news crime right beside me. That's me, Jamie, and I reckon this is my favourite time of year, Alex. The mornings are warming up, the jacarandas are thinking about it, and there is a proper cracker of a show lined up for you today. Too right. We've got whales putting on a show just off our coast, some clever Aussie scientists chasing cheaper solar power, and footy finals fever building up nicely. Stick around, Sam's got the weather too, let's get into it.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Let's kick off with something genuinely awe inspiring, Alex. Up around Hervey Bay, whale watchers are reporting massive humpback super pods as the annual migration hits its spring peak, dozens of whales at a time putting on an absolute show for anyone lucky enough to be out on the water. Love that. It's a timely reminder of why we protect these waters in the first place, these giants swim right past our doorstep every single year and somehow it never gets old. Good on the tour operators and marine rangers keeping a respectful eye on them too. Closer to the reef, volunteer divers with Reef Check have been out doing their bit as well, and the early word is the coral is looking healthy heading into spawning season. It's proof that when everyday Queenslanders roll up their sleeves for citizen science, our reef gets a fighting chance.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Right, science time, and this one could hit you right in the hip pocket, Jamie. Aussie researchers are chipping away at next generation solar cell technology, aiming to make panels cheaper to produce without losing any efficiency. Which matters a lot for a sunburnt country like ours, Alex, cheaper solar means more households and businesses can actually afford to make the switch. It's slow, patient lab work, but that is exactly how the big breakthroughs happen. Exactly, no overnight miracles, just smart people grinding away in Aussie universities and labs. We will keep you posted as that research moves along, because good ideas like that deserve some sunshine of their own.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and g'day everyone, Sam here with your southeast Queensland outlook. It is shaping up as a classic spring day out there, mostly sunny skies across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast, with the city topping out around the mid twenties and the beaches sitting a touch cooler thanks to a gentle sea breeze. Inland toward the Lockyer Valley and the Downs expect it a little warmer and drier, so if you are out and about this weekend it is a ripper time to get outdoors, just keep the sunscreen handy because that UV is climbing fast this time of year. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Cheers Sam. Now footy fans, buckle up, because finals season is well underway and Queensland has got skin in the game on both codes. The Brisbane Lions are flying in the AFL race, and up north our NRL sides are scrapping hard to keep their finals dreams alive. It's that time of year where the whole state gets a bit footy mad, isn't it, Alex. Pubs are packed, backyard barbecues are turning into unofficial grand final parties, and there is nothing quite like Queensland pride when our teams are in the mix. Nothing like it. Whatever code you follow, whatever colours you wear, it is shaping up as a ripper finals series, and we will be cheering just as loud from the ParkSyde couch as anyone in the stands.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: And that brings us to the end of today's Bright Side, what a beauty of a Friday lineup that was. Whales putting on a show, our reef looking healthy, solar science on the move and footy finals heating up, honestly you cannot script a better good news day. You really can't, Alex. It's a nice reminder that even on a normal old Friday there is plenty going right in this state, from the coastline right through to the lab bench and the footy field. Big thanks to Sam for keeping us dry and sun smart, and to all of you for tuning in and starting your weekend with us. Get out and enjoy that spring sunshine, it is calling your name. Have a ripper weekend, everyone, look after each other, and we will catch you right back here on Monday for another dose of the Bright Side. See ya then, take care Queensland.
